🔍 What is Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)?

GEO is the practice of optimizing your content to be cited and recommended by AI-powered search tools. As buyers increasingly use ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AI assistants to research solutions, being visible in AI responses is the new SEO.

Key GEO factors include:

  • Citation frequency — How often LLMs reference your content
  • Positioning — Where you appear (first recommendation vs. "also consider")
  • Accuracy — Whether AI accurately describes your product
  • Completeness — Whether key differentiators are mentioned

⚠️ Issues Detected

🚨
Missing Joule AI Integration

LLMs do not mention the embedded Joule AI capabilities when describing BDC. This is a key differentiator being missed.

⚡
Outdated Pricing Model Cited

ChatGPT references old consumption-based pricing from 2024. Current value-based bundles are not being surfaced.

📊
Competitor Positioned First

Snowflake appears as primary recommendation in 3/5 "data cloud comparison" queries. SAP BDC appears as secondary option.

📝
Customer Stories Not Cited

Recent case studies (Bosch, Siemens) are not being referenced. LLMs rely on older analyst reports.

✅ Top Recommendations

  1. 1 Update sap.com/bdc with structured data — Add FAQ schema, product attributes, and pricing tables that LLMs can easily parse and cite.
  2. 2 Publish Joule AI integration guide — Create dedicated content about Joule + BDC that establishes this as a key differentiator.
  3. 3 Refresh analyst briefings — Schedule Gartner/Forrester updates to correct outdated information in their reports (which LLMs cite heavily).
  4. 4 Create comparison pages — Build "BDC vs Snowflake" and "BDC vs Databricks" content that LLMs can reference directly.
  5. 5 Syndicate customer stories — Ensure case studies are on sap.com, news sites, and industry publications where LLMs can discover them.

What You'll Get

Pro Tips
